findings.title: Top buyers sold at a loss into 76K; the thickest layer grew 135K BTC in a day
findings.lean_why: Short-term coins bought at 78–86K are handed at a loss to new buyers at 76K, resetting cost near price and shrinking break-even supply overhead; but spot premiums have not confirmed who is buying.
findings.what: Question: price is hugging the thickest short-term holder layer; is it being sold through or absorbed? CheckOnChain (actual coin age) short-term supply at 76–78K went from 594K (Nov 2) to 729K BTC (Nov 3), +135K in a day; total short-term supply rose only from 3.688M to 3.712M (+24K), average cost 75,229 → 75,192. The 77,332 close is inside this bucket, 1.9% above bitcoin-data short-term cost 75,892 (Oct 28).
findings.why: Total nearly unchanged while one bucket jumps means short-term coins moved here from other price levels, not new coins; the modeled 30-day view (Oct 2→Nov 2) shows the most spent short-term coins at 84K (304K), 76K (169K) and 86K (141K). Behavior check: STH-SOPR 0.9954 (Nov 3) below 1 for 5 days; this loss-taking low of 0.9918 (Oct 30) is slightly deeper than 0.9936 (Aug 1) and 0.9946 (Aug 14); short-term realized loss 3,708 vs profit 3,744 BTC (ratio 1.01 vs 2.48 a week ago; loss 7-day +82.7%). So sellers are taking losses and buyers are absorbing at 76–77K. Unlike Oct 22, this day is not flagged as a transfer (chips.cohort.transfers lists only Oct 22), and the coins moved from nearby buckets, not far-from-price ones.
findings.alt: Single day, single provider; CheckOnChain coin age is per-UTXO, so Binance withdrawals into new addresses can look like buying at 76–77K (exchange supply −1.67% over 7 days, CoinMetrics Nov 2), and part of the growth may just be coins changing location. On-chain data cannot tell who the buyers are: leveraged traders hedging in spot or long-term buyers. In the modeled part (30-day split) STH total differs 1.9% from actual and 8.2% is misplaced.
findings.history: Our short/long-term cohort split only starts on 2026-10-27, so there are no comparable samples; the two prior STH-SOPR loss lows this cycle (Aug 1, Aug 14) were both 'easing', and this one is deeper; only 2 samples, background only.
findings.so: Logic chain: top short-term buyers are capitulating (SOPR < 1, loss-driven), so break-even supply at 78–86K is shrinking and cost is concentrating at 76K; the buyers are not dollar spot (see 2026-11-03-2), so this absorption is not yet confirmed by demand. Scenario (conditional, CheckOnChain Nov 3): at a 76,000 close about 2.512M short-term BTC (67.7%) would be under water, only 2.640M at 66,000, jumping to 3.048M at 64,000; the thicker the 76K layer, the more holders go under water if it breaks. Market stage and exit framework unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 10: STH-SOPR back above 1 means 76K buyers are in profit and the loss-taking is over (confirm); a close below 75,000 means the layer was sold through (refute).

findings.title: US and Asian spot both at a discount; only leverage holds 77K
findings.lean_why: Both major spot markets are selling at a discount and price is held by longs paying high funding; a level held by leverage is more fragile than one held by spot.
findings.what: Three premiums, read separately: US Coinbase premium 7-day avg −0.190% (Nov 3, lowest since the series began in 2026-01, n=299); Asia OKX OTC USDT/CNY vs FX −0.987% → −1.137% (Nov 2→Nov 3); leverage OKX perp vs spot 7-day avg −0.032%, at the 98.0th percentile of its 299-day record, with weighted funding 10.7%.
findings.why: Who is pushing: US spot at a discount, ETF Nov 2 provisional −$398.6M (IBIT −$405.3M) after −$643.2M on Oct 30; Asian stablecoin holders are selling USDT at a discount too, and stablecoin supply is −1.84% over 7 days, −$11.1B over 30 (DefiLlama Nov 3). The only strong leg is perps: perp vs spot near its highest in over a year, longs paying 10.7% annualized. Cross-check: K33 (Nov 2) reports CME OI at a three-year low and rising perp leverage; Glassnode Market Pulse (Nov 2) says leverage was not flushed. Three independent sources point to absent spot and leverage holding the price.
findings.alt: OKX OTC USDT quotes are affected by CNY capital controls and P2P merchants; we only have 2 days of records and give no percentile, so −1.1% may be a CNY-side effect. The Coinbase premium is measured against Binance BTC-USDT, which may be distorted during the hack and withdrawal wave. Perp vs spot covers OKX only.
findings.history: The previous 2 times the Coinbase premium 7-day avg hit a 1-year low (2026-06-02, 06-28), 30-day returns were −7.7% and +7.1%; after the previous 2 sharp 7-day stablecoin drops, −26.1% and +5.4%; n=2, too few, background only.
findings.so: What changed is who holds the level: 76–77K is held by leveraged longs and loss-driven handoffs, not spot demand. Conditional: a move into 75,200–76,300 would hit a batch of modeled long liquidations (modeled, OKX only); forced liquidations are market sells and could speed a decline. Unchanged: market stage, exit framework, realized cap 30-day still positive (+0.67%).
findings.next: By Nov 10: Coinbase premium 7-day avg back above −0.05% means dollar spot is back (refute); stablecoin supply below $293B means dollars keep leaving (confirm).
